common_name: Primrose Star Clematis Montana (Semi-Double Creamy-Yellow Star-Shaped Spring Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Primrose Star is a compact 'Mini Montana' selection that flowers on the previous year's growth and should be pruned only right after flowering, if at all (Group 1).

directions: Bred in New Zealand in the 1990s, Primrose Star stands apart from other Clematis montana forms with unusual semi-double, star-shaped flowers whose narrow, slightly twisted tepals open creamy primrose-yellow and fade toward white as they age. It blooms in a single flush in late spring on wood made the previous year, so any pruning should be limited to tidying right after flowering. Its noticeably more restrained size compared to rampant montana types makes it a better fit for a modest fence, garage wall, or large container.

common_name: Continuity Clematis Montana (Repeat-Flowering Pink Spring-to-Fall Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Continuity begins blooming as the main montana flush fades and keeps producing flowers over the summer, so prune only lightly right after the first main flush.

directions: Unlike most Clematis montana selections, which deliver one overwhelming spring flush and then rest, Continuity opens its soft pink flowers just as that main crop is finishing and continues producing waves of bloom through summer into early fall. Older flowers give way to fluffy grey seed heads that mingle attractively with the later flushes still opening nearby. This extended season of interest, paired with the vigorous climbing habit typical of the montana group, makes it a useful choice for covering a large wall, pergola, or tree where a single spring show would otherwise leave months of bare green foliage.

common_name: Snowbird Clematis Macropetala (Double White Nodding Atragene Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Snowbird is a compact macropetala type suited to smaller supports and needs no regular pruning.

directions: Raised by English clematis breeder Barry Fretwell, Snowbird produces fully double, pure white, nodding bell-shaped flowers with long twisted inner tepals, opening in mid-spring on the previous year's growth and often again more lightly in late summer on new wood. Like other Atragene-group clematis it needs no routine pruning beyond removing dead stems and a light shaping right after the main spring bloom. Its compact habit and clean white double flowers suit a small obelisk, trellis, or large container near a path where the blooms can be seen up close.

common_name: Ladakh Clematis (Rare Yellow Nodding Himalayan Species Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; this high-altitude Himalayan species flowers on growth made earlier the same season and needs only light shaping after bloom.

directions: Native to the cold, arid mountains of Ladakh and the western Himalaya into southwestern Tibet, this rare species clematis carries finely divided, narrow, glaucous-blue leaflets and small nodding flowers that open bell-shaped before flaring into an angel-wing form, colored yellow and often flushed or spotted with purplish brown on the outside. A specialist plant found mainly through collectors and alpine or species-clematis nurseries rather than mainstream garden centers, it is best given sharply drained, lean soil that echoes its native scree and rock-crevice habitat, with some afternoon shade from the hottest sun in warmer gardens. Its scarcity in cultivation and distinctive flower form make it a curiosity for Clematis collectors rather than a general-purpose garden vine.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online
